title: ARE DILEMMAS AND CONFLICTS IN LLM ALIGNMENT SOLVABLE? A VIEW FROM PRIORITY GRAPH

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual analysis and theoretical formalization using priority graphs to illustrate how models implicitly favor specific moral frameworks (e.g., consequentialist vs. deontological ethics) in classic dilemmas like the Trolley Problem.

Qualitative examination and directed graph modeling of how models prioritize competing, positive human values (e.g., environmental sustainability vs. economic value; truthfulness vs. protection from harm) in given contexts.

Theoretical evaluation of subjective alignment challenges, using qualitative examples (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge evaluating artworks or stories) to demonstrate how models navigate conflicting, non-factual human tastes and aesthetic preferences.
